sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for saved decks
sections.what: Brings in the database helpers and the run and stage tables, the deck type, and the shared error type from the reality-scan deck store.
sections.why: Likely reason: the shared error type keeps error messages consistent with the other deck store.
sections.watch_out: Long relative and cross-package imports break if either folder moves.

sections.name: getLessonsDeck
sections.title: Loading the saved deck
sections.what: Loads the deck saved for a run. It reports not found if the run is missing, and a conflict error if the deck stage did not succeed or holds no deck.
sections.why: Stated in the comment: the deck lives inside the run and is never sent elsewhere.
sections.watch_out: A run whose deck build failed shows a conflict message asking for a rerun of the deck stages.

sections.name: saveLessonsDeck
sections.title: Saving edits safely
sections.what: Saves a changed deck with a new revision number, but only if the stored revision still matches the one the editor started from. If not, it refuses and asks the user to reload.
sections.why: Stated in the comment: a revision compare-and-swap prevents two edits from overwriting each other.
sections.watch_out: The whole summary is overwritten, so any other data stored beside the deck in that stage is lost on save.

summary: Loads and saves the editable slide deck for a Lessons Learnt run, stored inside that run's record in the database.
purpose: Lets a user review and change the deck for one run without changing the shared source data.
why: Stated in the comment: edits and approvals stay inside the run and are never written to the Yard, and saves use a revision check.
how: getLessonsDeck finds the run, then reads its scene_deck stage. It returns the saved deck only if that stage succeeded and holds one. saveLessonsDeck writes a new deck with the revision number increased by one, but only if the stored revision still matches the one the editor started from. If no row matched, it reports a conflict.
inputs: A run id for loading. A deck and the revision number the editor started from for saving.
outputs: The stored deck for loading, or the updated deck with its new revision and timestamp for saving. Errors are returned as DeckError with a status code.
risks: Saving replaces the whole stage summary with the deck and slide count, so any other data kept there is lost. The revision check depends on the stored revision being a number.
debug: A 404 means the run id is wrong. A 409 on load means the deck stage did not succeed or is missing, so rerun the deck stages. A 409 on save means someone else saved first, so reload and retry. If saves always fail, check the stored summary's revision value in the database.
